verdicts.verify_by: bash tests/b2-reach-typename-flat-gas.sh from a clone at 58b269206: compare per-iteration gas and wall deltas of short vs 60 KB type name; also the Go bench tests/b2-reach-typename-flat-gas_test.go copied into gnovm/cmd/calibrate, -bench 'Reflect_ObjectInfo_(Stamped$|TypeName)'
verdicts.tldr: The row comment's 'nothing here scales with caller input' is false, since the type name is concatenated per call, but gas tracks the extra work within about 1.5x, not several times
verdicts.details: declaredTypeName returns dt.PkgPath + "." + string(dt.Name) on every stamped call (reflect.go:143), so the work grows with a type name the caller declares, while the objectInfo row is SizeFlat and its comment says nothing scales with caller input. The returned string is charged allocation gas, so gas does rise with the name: +9,740 gas per call for a 60 KB name. Three reruns of the finder's script measured 0.62-0.63 ns/gas for the short name and 0.71-0.91 ns/gas for the 60 KB name, about 0.84-1.25 ns/gas at the margin. That gap is within 1.5x of the base rate and does not reproduce the finder's 2.3-3.6 ns/gas or the claim that a block runs several times longer than its gas. What remains is a row comment that misdescribes the native. Fix: reword the native_gas.go row comment to say the type-name string grows with the declared name and is covered by allocation gas, or have the calibrate bench add a long-name case.

verdicts.verify_by: cp tests/b1-reach-conversion-splits-object.gno gnovm/tests/files/zrealm_reflect_conversion.gno && go test ./gnovm/pkg/gnolang -run 'TestFiles/zrealm_reflect_conversion.gno' -count=1: expect 'same object equal: true', observe false | cp tests/b1-catalog-object-type-varies.gno gnovm/tests/files/zrealm_reflect_b1_typevaries.gno && go test ./gnovm/pkg/gnolang -run 'TestFiles/zrealm_reflect_b1_typevaries' -v; the pinned Output passes with `a == b: false a == c: false` and `distinct keys for one object: 3`
verdicts.tldr: Converting the pointer before calling Of gives one persisted object two unequal Objects and a type chosen by the caller, so dedup or map keys by Object can count it twice
verdicts.details: X_objectInfo derives id and addr from the heap item that ownObject resolves, but it takes typ from declaredTypeName(v) (reflect.go:37), which reads tv.T, the static type of the pointer the caller passed. So Of(tok) and Of((*Alias)(tok)) carry the same id and address but different typ. Object is a struct of four strings compared field by field, so the two compare unequal. This breaks the doc's promise at reflect.gno:47, 'Two Objects are equal if and only if they name the same object' and 'safe as a map key'. The same thing happens across packages, with type Mine strings.Builder over a *strings.Builder. Fix: take typ from the heap item's own value type (hiv.Value.T) rather than the argument's static type, or drop typ from the compared struct, and pin the equality with a filetest.
verdicts.evidence: In a scratch worktree at 58b269206, go test -run 'TestFiles/zrealm_reflect_conversion.gno$' with the finder's file failed with the actual output '+same object equal: false', '+map entries for one object: 2', '+type via alias: gno.land/r/demo/reflectconv.Alias', '+cross-package equal: false', '+type via Mine: gno.land/r/demo/reflectconv.Mine'. Merge base: gnovm/stdlibs/chain/reflect does not exist, so the PR introduces this.

verdicts.verify_by: cp tests/b3-claims-object-equality.gno gnovm/tests/files/zrealm_b3claims_equality.gno && cd gnovm/pkg/gnolang && go test -run 'TestFiles/zrealm_b3claims_equality' -count=1 . ; it passes at head with 'a == b: false a == c: false' and 'map entries for one object: 3'
verdicts.tldr: The documented equality and map-key guarantee fails: one object read through *Token, *Alias and *struct{ n int } gives three Objects with one address
verdicts.details: declaredTypeName begins with t := tv.T (reflect.go:128), the argument's static pointer type, so the typ field follows whatever pointer type the caller converted to. A conversion to an unnamed struct pointer even gives typ "". The three Objects have the same Address() and ok is true for each, yet they compare unequal and take three slots in a map[reflect.Object]bool. That contradicts 'Two Objects are equal if and only if they name the same object' at reflect.gno:47. A realm that registers or dedupes by Object therefore admits the same object again under each pointer type. This is the same root cause as candidate 6 and is to be reconciled with it. Fix: read the type from the heap item's own TypedValue in X_objectInfo, which also makes the type P *Token unwrap unnecessary.
